paper.title_en: Noninertial Reference Frames in Special Relativity
paper.abstract_en: Although the special theory of relativity was conceived to relate inertial reference frames, it is not generally known by beginning students, or even by academics not specializing in general relativity, that it can be applied to noninertial reference frames. The general perception among non-specialists seems to be that noninertial reference frames can only be described through general relativity. This situation has led to some controversy regarding the necessity of general relativity to address problems involving accelerated systems, such as the twin paradox and the description of rotating reference frames. We discuss the controversy and propose that, to avoid the present confusion, the local validity of special relativity in the absence of gravitation, despite the use of noninertial frames, should be explicitly and clearly stated at an early stage of the learning process.
